purpose: Bicalutamide is used to treat prostate cancer. It is often used together with other treatments to help slow or stop the growth of prostate cancer cells. It works by blocking male hormones that can fuel cancer growth.
how_it_works: Prostate cancer cells often need a male hormone called testosterone to grow. Bicalutamide works by blocking the places on cancer cells where testosterone tries to attach, like putting a plug in a lock. Without testosterone being able to connect to those cells, the cancer has a harder time growing and spreading.
common_side_effects: Hot flashes (sudden feelings of warmth or flushing), breast tenderness or swelling, decreased sex drive, mild nausea, tiredness, and dizziness are the most common side effects. Some men also notice mild swelling in the legs or mild stomach upset.
warnings: This medicine can sometimes cause liver problems, so your doctor will check your liver with blood tests regularly. Tell your doctor right away if you notice yellowing of your skin or eyes, dark urine, or severe stomach pain. It should NOT be used by women who are pregnant. Also let your doctor know about all other medicines you take, as bicalutamide can interact with certain blood thinners like warfarin.
typical_dosing: The most common dose is one 50 mg tablet taken by mouth once a day, at the same time each day. It is usually taken together with another medicine called a LHRH analog. Some patients may be prescribed a higher dose of 150 mg once daily depending on their specific situation. Always follow your doctor's instructions exactly.
